subject: Pricing tranching & make-good structure for Pinecrest Health — VP/CFO clearance
messages:
From: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 14 Feb 2029 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Pricing tranching proposal for Pinecrest Health — signoff needed

Team,

Summary: Pinecrest (large regional health system) is asking for an aggressive onramp package to get a 12‑month pilot live quickly. They want an up‑front 25% list discount on our hosted API rates for year 1 plus a make‑good credit tied to utilization in Q2 that could convert into a permanent blended effective price if volume holds. The sales ask is time‑boxed and driven by a procurement deadline next week (02/21).

Why: procurement says they need predictable unit economics for their CFO to approve the PO. The customer is otherwise ready to sign a 12‑month pilot and commit to a joint press reference. We estimate a $430k TCV for the pilot if accepted.

What I need from finance/pricing: VP/CFO clearance for an exception to standard discount guardrails (this would be outside our 20% threshold and introduce a conditional make‑good). Specifically:
- Approve an initial effective discount up to 25% for Y1 with a clearly capped make‑good credit if utilization exceeds the pilot forecast.
- Confirm acceptable aggregate credit cap and clawback language acceptable to finance.

Attachments: pricing‑calcs.xlsx (breakdown of unit economics), draft‑MAP.pdf (mutual action plan).

I can rework to a one‑time onboarding credit instead of a recurring list discount if that simplifies approval — happy to adapt. Need a decision by EOD Friday so we can hit procurement's deadline.

Thanks,
Laura
Laura Bennett
Enterprise Sales, Redwood Inference
[attachment: pricing-calcs.xlsx (spreadsheet, 78 KB)]
[attachment: draft-MAP.pdf (pdf, 220 KB)]

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>
To: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 14 Feb 2029 10:03:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Pricing tranching proposal for Pinecrest Health — signoff needed

Laura —

Thanks for the context and the calcs; quick Qs before I can recommend to Markus:
1) How durable is the 25% discount — is it applied across all usage or just to a capped tranche for the pilot months?
2) The make‑good as written looks like it could convert to a permanent price if volume hits forecast — can we instead structure a refundable onboarding credit (one‑time) that scales with usage? That keeps list pricing intact and avoids rate precedent.
3) What is the churn/contract risk if they terminate at month 6 — do we have clawback language?

If the sales case includes an explicit cap on aggregate credits and a 6‑month clawback window, I’m comfortable supporting a narrower exception.

-Kim
Senior Pricing Manager
[inline: looked at pricing-calcs.xlsx]

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>
Cc: Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 14 Feb 2029 11:47:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Pricing tranching proposal for Pinecrest Health — signoff needed

Team —

I reviewed the pipeline and Pinecrest is strategic for our health vertical presence in the Midwest. I back Laura on moving quickly, but agree with Kim that we should protect revenue and precedent. Proposed compromise:
- Replace an ongoing 25% list discount with a one‑time onboarding credit equal to the first 3 months of expected consumption (scale tiers attached).
- Cap total credits at $150k.
- If they renew beyond 12 months we can revisit a long‑term discount as part of renewal economics.

I've attached a short executive analysis that models ARR impact under three adoption scenarios. If Markus signs off on the $150k cap + 6‑month clawback, we can give Pinecrest a clear yes and push legal to add the clawback clause.

Marissa
VP, Strategic Accounts
[attachment: exec-escrow-analysis.pdf (pdf, 52 KB)]

From: Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.com>
To: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 14 Feb 2029 14:10:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Pricing tranching proposal for Pinecrest Health — signoff needed

Thanks — I appreciate the framing and the willingness to reduce precedent risk. A few finance asks before I can give formal signoff: 
1) Credit cap: set at $150,000 aggregate (approval condition).
2) Clawback: prorated clawback if they terminate before month 7, recoverable across a 6‑month window.
3) Term: Pilot stays at 12 months; any discount conversion requires an explicit renewal negotiation (no auto‑convert clause).
4) Legal: add explicit language for clawback and for proof of usage (we accept our usage logs as official metric).

If you can update the pricing‑calcs to show net present value with the $150k cap and the clawback scenario (best/likely/worst), I’ll review and provide a signoff note to include in the redlined commercial memo to Pinecrest. I want the memo to explicitly state this is an exception and list the internal approvers.

I don’t see a need to route to the CFO beyond me for this size, but legal review is required before we present to Pinecrest procurement.

-Markus
VP, Finance (Acting CFO)
[inline: please update the spreadsheet and send back]

From: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
To: Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>
Cc: Sara Gomez <sara.gomez@pinecresthealth.com>, Pinecrest Procurement <procurement@pinecresthealth.com>
Date: Wed, 14 Feb 2029 16:45:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Pricing tranching proposal for Pinecrest Health — signoff needed

Markus / team —

Thanks for the quick review. Attached is an updated workbook (pricing‑calcs‑updated.xlsx) showing the three adoption scenarios with the $150k cap and a modeled clawback (6‑month prorated). I also removed the auto‑convert clause and replaced the proposed recurring discount with a tiered, refundable onboarding credit.

Next steps I propose:
- Markus confirms signoff note (I’ll embed it in the commercial memo).
- Legal drafts the clawback and usage verification language (I’ll loop in Legal and send draft to Pinecrest).
- Once legal clears, I’ll present the memo to Sara and procurement and request PO by 02/21.

Sara / Pinecrest team — we’re prepared to move forward on the revised structure if this aligns with your procurement guidelines. Happy to hop on a 30‑minute call tomorrow to walk through the numbers.

Laura
Laura Bennett
Enterprise Sales, Redwood Inference
[attachment: pricing-calcs-updated.xlsx (spreadsheet, 85 KB)]
